key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed joint geometry combined with optimized DDFW settings substantially improves AA2024-T351 weld strength, while deep learning can predict tensile performance from process parameters.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical route to stronger lightweight aerospace/automotive aluminum joints by pairing geometry-driven mechanical interlocking with AI-guided process optimization.
method: L18 orthogonal array tested friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying surface geometry, and friction time.
Compared conventional flat-to-flat joints against a novel drilled-to-bossed geometry in direct drive friction welding.
Trained deep learning models to predict ultimate tensile strength from welding conditions.
evidence_signal: The best condition (30 MPa friction pressure, 70 MPa forging pressure, 2200 rpm, drilled-to-bossed geometry, 4 min friction time) achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, and the top model reached R² ≈ 0.81.
watch_item: The predictive model accuracy is moderate rather than near-perfect, so broader validation on more datasets and operating conditions would be needed before deployment.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
